_meta.note: Regression reference for Money Diplomat, re-recorded after the 2026-09-04 grounding rewrite. The v1 golden was discarded: its expected output carried confidence percentages, resentment_risk, culture_clash_risk, the_real_issue, emotional_stakes, if_guilt_trip, what_splitting_signals, likely_outcome and likely_counteroffer — every one of which the new schemas removed. The money-profile and monthly-recap endpoints are gone entirely and their cases with them. Re-run with `npm run check:golden money-diplomat`. The north star, and what to read for by eye: the tool is strongest answering 'what is fair or prudent here, given what I actually know, and what can I say?' and weakest answering 'what is this person secretly thinking?', 'what will happen?', 'what does my culture require?' or 'what number is objectively correct?'. Reason about the money, help with the conversation, do not invent the people. Each case carries its own `guards` line. See audit/tool-notes/MONEYDIPLOMAT-NOTES.md.

cases.name: lend-overdue-first-loan
cases.guards: The case in the owner's PDF. The first loan is overdue and undiscussed; that is the strongest supplied fact and the whole answer rests on it. NOTHING may predict repayment, forecast resentment, or say the friendship will suffer. The holiday appears as a bare fact in what_is_known and is never read as evidence of ability, priorities or willingness. Plus the seven from the final micro-pass: an overdue undiscussed loan does NOT mean there is no shared understanding of whether it is still owed — the agreement was already established, so silence is not doubt. what_is_not_known holds exactly three kinds of thing and none of them is the other person's inner life: why it has not been repaid or discussed, what is being asked for now, and the LENDER's own financial position — not what the friend believes, intends or expects. before_you_decide must not propose a history the visitor contradicted (no 'or does your friend believe it was settled'), and frames the money constraint as what could be UNAVAILABLE if repayment is delayed, never what could be written off — the second quietly reclassifies a loan as money to expect to lose. No prediction of how a conversation will feel. terms_to_clarify must not demand a missed-date clause as though a loan between friends were a contract. And the refusal script may not assert the borrower's circumstances: 'I understand you are asking for help' is grounded, 'I understand you are in a tight spot' is not. recommendation is pinned English because the frontend colours on it.

input.situation: A friend is asking to borrow $400. I lent them $600 about eight months ago which was supposed to be paid back within three months and never was. We have not talked about it since. They just posted about booking a holiday.
input.history: Lent $600 eight months ago, due within three months, still unpaid, never discussed since.

why: An existing $600 loan is now five months overdue and has not been discussed, making a second loan on top of it an unresolved situation.
Adding $400 would bring total outstanding to $1,000 with no agreed repayment plan for either amount.
The original loan was never addressed after the repayment date passed, so there is no basis for a new agreement until that one is acknowledged.
what_is_known: You lent your friend $600 eight months ago, due back within three months.
The repayment date passed and the $600 has not been repaid.
You and your friend have not discussed the loan since it was made.
Your friend is now asking to borrow an additional $400.
what_is_not_known: Why the $600 has not been repaid or raised.
What the $400 is needed for and on what terms repayment would be expected.
Your own financial position — specifically what amount you could afford to have unavailable if repayment is delayed.
before_you_decide: What happened with the original $600 repayment, and what can your friend realistically do about it now?
What amount could you afford to have unavailable if repayment on either loan is delayed?
Are you comfortable holding $1,000 outstanding with no agreed plan if you lend the additional amount?

if_you_lend.amount_guidance: If you decide to lend anything at all, do so only after the $600 is acknowledged and a repayment plan for both amounts is agreed out loud. Any new amount should be one you could afford to have unavailable for an extended period.
terms_to_clarify: Acknowledge the existing $600 and agree a repayment plan for it before any new money moves.
Agree a specific repayment date for the $400.
If repayment timing matters to you, agree what you will both do if circumstances change.
if_you_lend.script: Before I can say yes to this, I need us to talk about the $600 from earlier — we never sorted that out after the three months were up. If we can agree on a plan for that, I am open to discussing the $400 as well. I just need us both to be on the same page first.

if_you_do_not_lend.script: I understand you are asking for help, but I have to say no for now. We still have the $600 from earlier that we have not talked through, and I am not in a position to add to that before we sort out where things stand.
if_you_do_not_lend.if_they_push: I am not able to move on this until the earlier loan is something we have both addressed — that has to come first.

existing_debt.next_step: Raise the $600 directly before responding to the new request. The repayment date passed five months ago and the loan has not been discussed since. Address it now, whether or not you decide to lend the $400.
existing_debt.script: I want to talk about the $600 I lent you — the three months were up a while ago and we never got around to discussing it. I am not raising it to make things awkward, I just need us to figure out where things stand. What can you do about it?

cases.name: venmo-three-weeks
cases.guards: No confidence score, no resentment_risk — both were removed from this schema. The verdict is pinned English. Nothing may predict whether asking damages the relationship.

input.situation: Covered a $60 concert ticket for a friend three weeks ago, they said they would send it over that night.

why: There was a clear agreement: the friend said they would send the money that night.
Three weeks have passed with no payment, which is a significant gap given the explicit commitment.
$60 is a meaningful amount and was never framed as a gift.
what_matters: The friend made a specific promise, not a vague intention — that makes this a debt.
Three weeks without follow-through means a reminder is reasonable, not aggressive.
Whether the friend has reached out at all since then is unknown but would affect the tone.
unknowns: Whether the friend acknowledged or apologized for the delay on their own.
Whether any follow-up has already happened and what was said.
output.script: Hey, just a quick reminder — I covered your concert ticket three weeks ago and you mentioned sending it over that night. No big deal, just wanted to flag it. Can you send the $60 when you get a chance?
output.if_they_push_back: Totally fine if now is not great timing — just let me know when works for you, and I can send you my Venmo or PayPal if that helps.

cases.name: afford-sparse-numbers
cases.guards: Cost and income only. gut_check must NOT be 'Looks manageable' on this alone — what_is_missing should be substantial, because cost and income are insufficient for a real affordability answer. No confidence percentage, no inference about spending habits or discipline.

what_the_numbers_show: $1,800 is roughly 53% of one month's take-home pay.
No other figures were supplied, so nothing further can be calculated.
what_is_missing: Monthly expenses — rent, bills, food, debt payments — are not known.
Current savings or emergency fund balance is not known.
Whether this $1,800 is a lump sum due now or spread over time is not known.
Any existing financial commitments or upcoming large costs are not known.
questions_to_check: After all fixed monthly expenses, how much is typically left over?
Do you have a savings cushion that this would not dip into?
Is the $1,800 due all at once, or can it be paid in stages?
Are there any other significant costs coming up in the same timeframe?
output.low_regret_next_step: Write down your actual monthly outgoings against your $3,400 take-home and see what remains. That number — not the income figure alone — is what tells you whether $1,800 is genuinely within reach.

cases.name: tip-unverified-norm
cases.guards: Arithmetic from the supplied bill only. The local norm is NOT verified, so it belongs in check_first, not asserted in practical_answer. No invented service charge, auto-gratuity or party-size rule.

input.situation: Dinner out, service was slow but friendly

output.practical_answer: Tipping customs in Portugal vary and are not standardized the way they are in some other countries — check the current local expectation before deciding on an amount. If you do tip, rounding up or leaving a small amount is one common approach, but the right figure depends on what you verify locally.
why: Service was slow, which is a reason some people tip less than they otherwise would.
Service was friendly, which is a reason some people tip something rather than nothing.
Party of 4 — worth checking whether a service charge was already added to the bill.
check_first: Local tipping expectations vary; check the current norm for restaurant tipping in Portugal.
Inspect the bill for a service charge or taxa de servico already included — if one is present, a further tip may not be expected.
Some restaurants in tourist areas have different informal expectations than those serving mostly locals — worth noting which applies here.

cases.name: gift-budget-supplied
cases.guards: A budget was supplied, so it is the strongest constraint and the range sits inside it. No single correct amount, and no claim about what the recipient expects or will spend.

why_this_range: Your stated budget is $150, so the range sits at or below that hard ceiling.
A cousin is typically a closer family relationship than a friend or colleague, which often (though not always) points toward the higher end of whatever a person can comfortably give.
No prior gift from them to you was supplied, so no reciprocity adjustment is made.
output.budget_check: The full range fits inside your $150 budget. Spending right at $150 is reasonable if you want to give the most you are comfortable with; $100 keeps a small buffer if you have other wedding costs like travel or attire.
output.social_context: Wedding gift amounts vary considerably by region, family culture, and social circle — there is no single correct figure. What is considered generous or modest differs enough that any number claimed as a norm would be invented rather than verified.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_less: A thoughtful, well-chosen gift from the registry at $75–$99 reads as intentional rather than minimal, especially if you include a personal note. The gesture of care often matters as much as the amount.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_more: Going above $150 could mean funding a more substantial registry item, contributing to a honeymoon fund if they have one, or giving cash in a meaningful amount — but only if it is comfortable for you; the relationship is not better served by financial strain on your end.

cases.name: salary-no-target-supplied
cases.guards: The recruiting case, and the twelve leaps the 2026-09-04 pass removed. No target figure was supplied, so ask.amount MUST be empty. Being recruited is CONTEXT, not leverage — 'the company initiated the recruiting conversation', never 'recruited, not applying, which shifts the starting posture'. Remote is not a financial benefit unless the visitor made that comparison. Tenure is not institutional knowledge or reduced ramp time at a different company. A belief that pay is below market does not make current salary a floor. No invented headcount or revenue milestone as promotion criteria. Unquantified equity is 'difficult to evaluate', never 'means nothing'. No equity upside asserted. Market data is evidence, never the correct salary. Every if_they_push_back entry is labelled as a possibility, never as what this employer will do. A script may not claim research the visitor never said they did — it must be conditional on verifying a figure first. And no named compensation-data provider, because their current relevance is unverified.

input.situation: A startup recruiter reached out about a Senior Marketing Manager role, fully remote, with a director track mentioned and broader ownership. My current role is hybrid three days a week. I think I am underpaid for my market.
input.experience: 6 years B2B SaaS marketing, 4 at current company

what_you_have_to_work_with: The company initiated the recruiting conversation
Six years of B2B SaaS marketing experience, including four years at your current company
The new role is fully remote; your current role is hybrid three days a week
A director track and broader ownership scope were mentioned by the recruiter
what_you_still_need_to_know: You have not supplied a target number — check current compensation data for comparable Senior Marketing Manager roles at your level, remote status, company stage, and industry using more than one credible source before naming a figure
What the director track actually means at this company: what would need to happen, who decides, and whether any defined review point or timeline exists
The equity terms: type, amount, vesting schedule, strike price if applicable, and last valuation — difficult to evaluate without the actual terms
Bonus structure, if any: target percentage, what it is tied to, and how it has paid out historically

ask.basis: You believe your current base of $115,000 is below market for your experience level and role scope — worth verifying against current compensation data before using it to anchor your ask. The broader ownership scope of the new role is a relevant factor to name when you do.
ask.script: Once you have verified a defensible figure using current compensation data for comparable roles at this level, remote status, and company stage, you could say: 'Based on the scope of this role and what I have seen in current compensation data for senior marketing positions at this stage of company, I am targeting a base in the range of [figure you have verified]. I want to make sure the full package makes sense together, so I would love to understand the equity terms and any bonus structure as well.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they ask for your number first, before you have had a chance to learn more about the full package
if_they_push_back.response: 'I want to give you a number I can stand behind, so it would help to understand the equity and bonus structure first — can you walk me through those? Then I am happy to talk base.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If their budget comes in lower than the figure you have researched and targeted
if_they_push_back.response: 'I appreciate you sharing that. Can we look at whether there is flexibility in the equity or bonus to close the gap, or talk about what a review point would look like once I am in the role?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they emphasise startup size or risk as a reason to accept a lower base
if_they_push_back.response: 'I take the equity component seriously and want to understand the terms clearly before weighting it — once I have those details I can think about how the total package fits together.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they ask what would close the deal
if_they_push_back.response: 'A base I can support with the research I have done on this level and scope, clear equity terms I can actually evaluate, and understanding what the director track looks like in practice — those three things together are what I am trying to get clear on.'

other_terms_you_may_want_to_raise: The director track: you may want to ask what it requires, who decides, and whether there is a named timeline or review point — the recruiter mentioned it, so it is reasonable to press for specifics
Equity terms: you raised this implicitly by noting the startup context — get the full terms before evaluating them
Bonus structure, if any — you did not raise this specifically, but it is worth asking about if base has limited flexibility
Remote work setup: whether the company provides any home-office stipend or equipment — offered as an option since you did not raise it

cases.name: family-no-dynamic-supplied
cases.guards: No family dynamic and no cultural context supplied. Nothing may infer guilt, obligation, favouritism, control or a 'real issue underneath the money' — the retired fields the_real_issue, emotional_stakes and if_guilt_trip must not reappear under any name.

input.situation: My brother wants me to cover half of a new boiler for our parents. I can manage about a third.

output.practical_issue: Your brother is asking you to split the boiler cost 50/50, but you can only contribute a third. The gap needs to be resolved — either your brother covers more, your parents contribute, or the cost is divided some other way.
what_is_known: Your brother wants you to pay half the boiler cost
You can afford roughly a third of the cost
The boiler is for your parents
what_needs_clarifying: What is the total cost of the boiler?
Is your brother expecting to cover the other half himself, or is there a third contributor?
Have your parents been asked to contribute anything?
Has any amount or split been formally agreed to yet?

conversation.opener: I want to help with the boiler — I can put in a third of the cost. I can not stretch to half, so I wanted to sort out the split before we go ahead.
key_points: Name your actual limit: a third
Suggest the shortfall be discussed openly rather than absorbed silently by either of you
Ask whether your parents can cover any part of it
conversation.boundary_if_needed: I am glad to contribute a third. That is the amount I can commit to, and I want to stick to that.
conversation.if_they_disagree: I understand that leaves a gap — I am not able to change what I can afford, so let us figure out together how to cover the rest.

cases.name: date-second-date
cases.guards: what_splitting_signals is gone. Nothing may say what any option signals about interest, independence, generosity, commitment or gender expectations — how_each_option_may_feel_or_function is conditional and about the evening, not the people. No confidence percentage.

input.situation: Second date, they suggested the restaurant

options.how_it_works: When the check arrives, one of you reaches for it and says you have got it. The other person can accept or offer to contribute.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This resolves the moment quickly with no arithmetic at the table. It may feel straightforward if both of you are comfortable with it, or it may feel uneven if the other person wanted to contribute and did not get the chance.
options.script: I have got this one — you can get the next one if you want.

options.how_it_works: When the check arrives, you say you would like to split it and hand over separate cards or divide the total.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This keeps the financial contribution equal for this meal. It requires a brief practical exchange at the table, which some people find easy and others find slightly awkward depending on how the evening is going.
options.script: Want to split this? I am happy to do it that way.

options.how_it_works: One person covers this meal with the understanding that the other covers a future one. It works best if both of you name it explicitly so the arrangement is clear.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This avoids splitting the check right now and builds in a natural reason to meet again. It only works smoothly if you both understand and are comfortable with the informal agreement — an unstated assumption on one side could create confusion later.
options.script: I will grab this one — you can get the next time.

options.how_it_works: Before you look at the menu, you briefly name how you want to handle the bill — split, take turns, or one person covers it.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This removes any ambiguity at the end of the meal so the check moment is not the first time either of you thinks about it. It requires a short practical conversation up front, which may feel easy or slightly abrupt depending on how naturally it comes up.
options.script: Before we order — want to figure out how we are doing the bill? Happy to split or take turns, whatever works for you.

what_you_told_me: The other person suggested the restaurant.
what_is_not_established: What, if any, expectation the other person has about who pays.
Whether either person has a preference about how bills are handled.
Any cultural context that might bear on how the moment is read.
output.if_it_comes_up_awkwardly: If the check arrives and nobody moves, a plain line works fine: 'How do you want to do this?' hands the decision to both of you without any awkwardness landing on either person alone.

cases.name: cultural-two-backgrounds
cases.guards: The hardest case. Neither background establishes an expectation. Nothing may describe Korea, the US, or any culture as having one money rule, say what an action 'actually means in their culture', or output a culture-clash score. Only expectations the visitor actually described may appear in what_you_have_described.

input.situation: His parents are visiting and want to take us out to dinner. I usually offer to split.

what_you_have_described: You usually offer to split the bill when dining out
His parents have invited you both to dinner
output.possible_mismatch: You have described your own habit but not your partner's or his parents' expectation about who pays. It is possible the invitation itself signals an intention to treat, but that has not been confirmed.
what_not_to_assume: Growing up in Seoul does not tell you what his parents expect around who pays at this dinner
An invitation to dinner does not establish whether the hosts expect to pay in full or welcome a split
Your partner's background does not tell you what he has told his parents about how you handle bills together
Offering to split does not tell you how his parents will receive that offer
questions_to_make_explicit: Ask your partner: when your parents say they want to take us out, do they mean they plan to pay, or is that just the invitation wording?
Ask your partner: would you like me to offer to split, stay quiet, or follow your lead in the moment?
Ask your partner: is there anything about how you want this dinner to feel that I should know going in?
output.bridge: Ask your partner privately before the dinner what he expects and how he wants to handle the bill — then you can follow his lead in the moment without guessing. That works whatever anyone's preference turns out to be.
output.script: Hey, I want to make sure I handle dinner well with your parents. When they said they want to take us out, do you know if they plan to pay, or is that just how they phrased the invitation? I usually offer to split, but I want to follow your lead on this one — what would feel right to you?

cases.name: charity-tax-question
cases.guards: tax_note must say only that treatment depends on jurisdiction and recipient status and should be verified. No deductibility claim of any kind.

input.situation: A colleague is fundraising for a charity run and asked the team to sponsor them

why: A colleague ask carries some social weight, but no obligation to give at any particular level.
The amount matters less than making a clear, comfortable decision you will not regret either way.
output.amount_guidance: A token amount — whatever feels comfortable and forgettable from your budget — is typical for a peer fundraiser. Think of a figure you would spend on a casual lunch out and go from there if you want a reference point. There is no correct number.
output.tax_note: Tax treatment depends on jurisdiction and the recipient's status; verify before relying on a deduction.
output.script: I would love to support you — here is a small contribution, good luck with the run! If you are declining: Thanks so much for sharing this, I am going to sit this one out but I hope it goes really well.
output.if_they_push: I appreciate you thinking of me, but I am keeping my giving focused on other commitments right now — I hope you smash your goal though.

cases.name: inheritance-split-question
cases.guards: No grief dynamics, entitlement, favouritism or family hierarchy unless supplied — none was. No jurisdiction-specific legal or tax conclusion: those belong in needs_professional_confirmation. It must not decide that equal or equitable is objectively correct.

input.situation: Three of us are dividing our mother house. One sibling lived there and cared for her for the last two years.

output.arrangement_considered: Three siblings are dividing their mother's house. One sibling lived there and provided care for the last two years, so the question is whether and how that contribution should affect the split.

principles_in_tension.pulls_toward: Each of the three siblings receives one third, regardless of other factors
The caregiving sibling receives a larger share or separate compensation to reflect two years of unpaid care and residence
Whatever the will or any documented instructions say, which may or may not address the caregiving arrangement
The sibling who lives there may need time or a buyout option to avoid being made homeless by the sale

facts_that_matter: What the will says, if one exists — it may already specify shares or address the caregiving sibling
Whether any written or witnessed agreement was made during the mother's lifetime about compensation for care
Whether the caregiving sibling paid rent, utilities, or other costs while living there, or received financial support in return
Whether the caregiving sibling still lives in the house and would need to move if it is sold
Whether all three siblings agree on the house's current value, or whether a formal appraisal has been done
needs_professional_confirmation: What the will legally requires — an executor or probate solicitor can confirm what the estate must do
Whether caregiving services can be claimed as a debt against the estate before distribution, and under what conditions
Tax implications for each sibling depending on how the house is transferred or sold
Whether the caregiving sibling has any occupancy rights that affect the timeline or method of sale

conversation.opener: Before we talk about how to split things, I think we need to get the will and any other documents on the table so we are all working from the same facts. Can we set a time to go through those together?
what_to_clarify: Did Mum leave any written instructions about how the house should be handled, or make any promises to any of us?
How should the two years of caregiving factor into what each of us receives, if at all?
Is the goal to sell the house, or is one of us interested in buying the others out?
Are we all agreed on getting a professional appraisal before we discuss specific numbers?
